h1: Domain and SSL set up so your site stays secure
overview: We point your domain at your site or app, set up the DNS records correctly and install an HTTPS certificate that renews on its own. desc:
Domain connection and SSL setup points your domain name at the right site or app and switches on HTTPS that renews itself. Ecom Swift LLC sets the DNS records, installs the certificate, fixes redirects and email records, and writes down every change.

## What is domain connection and SSL setup?

Domain connection means telling the internet where your domain lives, using DNS records. SSL setup means installing a certificate so visitors reach your site over HTTPS, with the padlock in the browser. Together they decide whether your address opens the right place, safely, every time.

DNS is a list of instructions held by your domain provider or DNS host. One wrong record can send visitors to an old server, break your email or make the site unreachable on one version of the address. Because the records look technical, many owners avoid touching them until something breaks.

## Why a careful setup matters

Browsers warn visitors when a site lacks a valid certificate or loads some content over plain HTTP. That warning stops people before they read a word. An expired certificate can take a working site to an error page overnight, often at a bad moment.

Email depends on DNS as well. Without proper SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, messages from your domain can land in spam or be rejected, including order confirmations and invoices. Search engines also treat the www and non-www versions of an address as separate unless one redirects to the other, which splits the signals that point to your site.

## How it supports trust and visibility

A clean domain setup supports the basics of a credible business. The padlock tells visitors their details are protected. One consistent address means links, bookmarks and search results all lead to the same place. Redirects from old pages keep earlier links useful after a move.

It also reduces maintenance. When certificates renew automatically and you are alerted before anything lapses, nobody has to remember a date. The records sheet we leave behind means the next person who changes hosting knows what each record is for.

## What a complete setup includes

- Domain connected to the correct site, app or hosting service.
- A and CNAME records set for the main address and subdomains.
- A certificate installed and configured to renew automatically.
- A redirect from www to non-www, or the reverse, in one agreed direction.
- Redirects for old URLs so earlier links still work.
- SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for email deliverability.
- Mixed content warnings found and fixed.
- Optional security headers, including HSTS, once everything works over HTTPS.
- A CDN or faster DNS service where it helps.
- A written sheet of all records, with a note on what each one does.

## How we work

We first check where the domain is registered, where DNS is hosted and where the site runs. We list the existing records and mark what is still needed. Changes are made in a careful order and timed so the site stays online while the records spread across the internet.

After the certificate is issued, we test the main address, the other version of it and key pages, and look for mixed content in the page source. For the larger packages we add email records, subdomains, a CDN, expiry alerts and help moving a domain between registrars. The three packages differ mainly in how many domains or subdomains are covered and how much of the extra security and email work is included.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the domain registered in your own name and account.
- Turn on auto-renewal for the domain itself.
- Use a single, agreed version of the address.
- Check email delivery after any DNS change.
- Keep a copy of your records before editing them.

**Avoid:**
- Deleting DNS records you do not recognize.
- Letting a certificate depend on one person's calendar reminder.
- Leaving old subdomains pointing at servers you no longer use.
- Forcing HTTPS headers before every page loads securely.
- Sharing your registrar password with a contractor.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who just bought a domain and cannot make it open their new site. It suits a business whose emails go to spam after a host change. It also suits a team that sees a browser warning on checkout or login pages.

## What we need from you

Tell us the domain name, where you bought it and where the site is hosted. If you cannot find your registrar, we can help identify it. We never need your passwords. Access is given as a delegate, team or limited user where your registrar or DNS host supports it, or you can make the record changes we list for you.
